rows.text: The prior round uploaded 30 manifest members and then wrote FINAL_BYTE_READBACK.json locally without a subsequent PUT; the pointer therefore described a readback that was not remotely readable. This round uploaded that exact pre-existing file (no time regenerated, payload readback_cn still 2026-10-25T01:30:50+08:00) and verified bytes+sha. No second finisher and no member re-upload.

The supplied driver was NOT rerun in this round; its accepted result is reused. Only this round's own read-only schema helper ran twice: once uncaptured, once captured. The captured output is byte-identical to the first, recorded in SCHEMA_EXAMINE_RERUN_EQUALITY.json.

The 20260831 and 20260901 RAW files carry an int64 0..299 axis with 300 distinct values. Per instruction it is recorded as an uninterpreted integer axis: it was not parsed as nanoseconds, not converted to dates, and no date was inferred from either filename. No alternate time field was substituted because none exists in these files.

The product directory was enumerated once inside the authorized bound and yielded 18 entries, all parquet, matching the retained file_index_ADJUST_FACTOR_CLEAN.json observation (n_files=18, observed 2026-08-10..2026-09-24). The count was recorded, not targeted.

No exact producer path for the adjust_factor_stock__incremental_* RAW files is supplied by any retained index or receipt, and this round did not expand the search. The finding is bounded as PRODUCER_NOT_IDENTIFIED_IN_RETAINED_INDEX; it is not a claim that no producer exists.

The registry row declares standard_required=[factor, fq], but none of the 21 measured files has a physical fq column. This is reported as a contract-vs-bytes difference only. fq was not added, inferred, or filled anywhere.

All 18 R33 adjust_factor files carry explicit timestamp[ns] single-date axes. 2026-08-31, 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 are absent from this layer; 2026-09-24 is present. Absence here is an observation about this one product directory, not a market-source absence claim.
